messages:
devon: Quick handoff — taking off in 10m, handing primary to @amanda. Short summary: we saw an embeddings eviction surge in eu-west starting 03:12UTC, caused by an autoscaler mis-eval + a sudden spike from customer X. Thundering rehydrate causing p95 token latency ~450ms, some 503s for a small cohort. Mitigations applied: bumped kv-ttl to 48h, routed heavy customers to graceful-degraded pool, and disabled aggressive scale-down policy. Current status: reduced errors, still monitoring p95.

sre-bot: Incident opened: INC-2026-0893 — embeddings-kv-evictions-eu-west. Pages: 3. Severity: Sev2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0893

amanda: ack, thanks @devon. I'll take primary. Can you drop the exact commands you ran so I can reproduce if it flares? Also who's secondary for next 2h?

devon: copying the commands I ran:

```bash
# bump ttl for embedding entries
redis-cli -h eu-west-redis01 CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy volatile-lru
redis-cli -h eu-west-redis01 EVAL "return redis.call('CONFIG','SET','maxmemory','12gb')" 0
# temporarily increase TTL on hot keys
python tools/kv_ttl_patch.py --region eu-west --pattern 'emb:*:hot' --ttl 172800
# route customer X to degraded pool
kubectl -n inference exec -it svc/router -- /bin/sh -c "reroute --customer X --pool degraded-eu-west"
```

devon: logs snippet showing spike:

```
[03:12:14] embeddings.kv.evict key=emb:U:12345 size=24MB
[03:12:14] request.id=req_93a4f - routing to primary pool - latency=1200ms
[03:12:15] autoscaler.scale_down from 8 -> 4 (reason: err metric stale)
```

jay: I saw the autoscaler health probe flapping around 02:58-03:05 UTC, looks like the control plane misread the metric window. Filed a small fix in infra: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pull/425

ops-lead: Noting customer impact: Customer X reported degraded responses in their EU cluster; CSM notified. No broad customer outage. Keep CS updated if errors > 5% over 15m.

amanda: Got it. I'm primary. Jay will be secondary for the next 2h. Actionables I'm taking now:
- validate TTL patch applied across all eu-west replicas (running diff)
- keep routing to degraded pool for heavy customers for +30m
- watch p95 and 5xx rate, will escalate to infra on any autoscaler abnormality

amanda: Running the validation command now:

```bash
# validate ttl change
python tools/kv_validate_ttl.py --region eu-west --expected-ttl 172800
# check replica sync
redis-cli -h eu-west-redis02 INFO replication | grep role
```

sre-bot: Reminder: runbook link for embeddings eviction: https://runbooks.redwood/embeddings/eviction (steps 1-6 are critical). Also: if >10% 5xx sustained for 10m, escalate to oncall@redwood.com and open a regional failover.

devon: TODOs for me before I leave:
- confirm the TTL diff across all nodes (done locally for node01/02, still pending node03)
- drop a short postmortem draft in the incidents tracker
- handover notes below

Handover notes (short):
- root cause: autoscaler mis-eval + single-customer spike
- mitigations in place: TTL bump, degraded routing, disabled scale-down window
- monitoring: dashboards -> Observability > Embeddings > eu-west > p95, 5xx-rate, eviction-rate
- runbook pointer: https://runbooks.redwood/embeddings/eviction
- escalation: contact infra oncall (pager: @jay) if autoscaler starts oscillating again

amanda: Thanks. I'll keep routing for +30m then re-evaluate. If things look green at 04:00UTC I'll start re-enabling scale-down with a conservative window.

pagerbot: Pager cleared for INC-2026-0893 at 03:46UTC. No active pages in last 20m.

jay: Quick note — infra PR 425 has a rollback guard. If autoscaler still misbehaves after TTL/warmup, we can temporarily pin the control-plane metric window to 90s.

amanda: Next checks before handoff to next shift (in 2h):
- p95 < 300ms and 5xx < 0.5% for 15m
- eviction rate trending down across all replicas
- ensure degraded pool has capacity to handle heavyweight customers

amanda: leaving my laptop open for 20m in case anyone needs a direct handover. If I step out, jay you've got secondary. :thumbsup:

devon: Leaving notes in the incident doc and linking runbook. TY all, handing over now. :wave:
